newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Meister - Banks need external regulation.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Meister - Banks need external regulation.

text.p: The Bundesbank directorate member responsible for bank supervision, Edgar Meister, said in remarks published on Thursday he welcomed proposals for more self-regulation by banks, but added an external supervisor remained essential.

Addressing the issue at a time when commercial banks are clamouring for a greater say in regulation, Meister said he was willing to talk to banks about new ideas, but said pure self-regulation would be a "risky experiment."
"The supervisor must take care to remain the lord of the proceedings," Meister said in an interview with the Handelsblatt daily newspaper. "The market itself does not see its own boundaries."
At the same time, Meister welcomed a recent initiative by the Group of Thirty leading commercial banks to draw up global standards on regulation as the "start of a new discussion."

Banks have criticised national supervision systems as inadequate for an era when many institutions operate globally and the distinction between banks and the so-called "non-banks" which also provide financial services becomes increasingly blurred.

Meister acknowledged there was a regulatory gap with regard to global bank activities, but said: "It cannot be in the interest of supervisory authorities to allow some global players to become independent."
